title: [MILL Senior Friday] World of Film with Mark Phelan
description:
Join us on Fridays for a day full of events for Seniors with the MILL @ MPL! All events are free and open to the public. Registration is recommended unless otherwise noted.


The White Ribbon (2009) | R

Using their social status and harsh punishments, a baron, a doctor and a pastor rule over a small German village. One day, the doctor falls off his horse after it trips over a wire strung between two trees. More pranks follow, seemingly without reason, all directed at the village's upper class and growing increasingly more brutal with time. There are no suspects, but a local schoolteacher has his suspicions.

ABOUT THE INSTRUCTOR
MARK PHELAN - I am a lifelong film fanatic who eats, breathes, sleeps and drinks movies. I have studied with Donald Spoto at the New School in NYC and have a BA and MA in Speech and Theatre from MSU. I have also worked as an actor and have directed several plays in local regional and community theaters, including the Whole Theatre in Montclair and the Paper Mill Playhouse in Millburn, NJ. I am currently working as an adjunct professor teaching, among other courses, Introduction to Cinema.

description:
At the Women’s Breakfast on Saturday, November 14, Tim Crist will discuss the research discoveries behind his book, New Englanders in a New Land, published by Rutgers University Press. In the book, Tim describes the way Congregationalists settled Newark in the 17th century and how they managed relationships with Native Americans and handled the question of slavery. 
Reviewers have commended Tim’s “impressive, pioneering research” and called the book “absorbing” in the way he “skillfully underscores the complexity of New Jersey’s origins by demonstrating how Newark’s leaders challenged the proprietary system in their quest to expand the New England model of godly authority and town self-government.” 
This program is open to everybody. 
Information about Tim’s book is available at: https://www.rutgersuniversitypress.org/new-englanders-in-a-new-land/9781978846883

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Verona Park
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK

We will meet at the benches in front of the boathouse.

We will walk the loop around the park. The goal will be at least three miles, but there is plenty of opportunity to stop or continue to fit your personal goals.

We will be walking on a **paved surface.**

We walk at a **medium speed**. As always, we will go at a moderate pace and won’t leave anyone behind. But **please be considerate** of others if you don't think you will be able to walk at a moderate pace for the duration.

Please plan to arrive 5 minutes **early** so that we can **start on time.**

Verona Park is 54.32 acres with a lake running through it. It is bordered by Lakeside and Bloomfield Avenues in the southern part of Verona. It is the fifth largest park in the Essex County system, making it a great place to walk.

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

description:
with Lea Peace & fellow members of Empty Cloud Monastery

Take a moment to re-center with instructors from the Empty Cloud monastery in this peaceful, contemplative yoga and meditation practice. About the presenter

title: Art Talk: Deborah Ugoretz
description:
https://deborahugoretz.com  
IG:@debugoretz  
@ketubah\_for\_life

Deborah Ugoretz is a master paper-cutter with 40 years of experience facilitating workshops and classes on Jewish paåpercutting and Hebrew illuminated manuscripts. Deborah has shown her work in galleries and museums across New York City and the US, and has served as a leader in artist communities as a curator for Yiddish New York and organizer of Red Hook Open Studios. In 2024, she was awarded a Folk Arts Fellowship by NY Council on the Arts and the New York Foundation for the Arts.  
  
Deborah shares her skill as an educator, most recently at the New School, National Yiddish Book Center, Yeshiva University Museum, the Museum at Eldridge Street, New York and at Fordham University where a retrospective of her cut paper work was exhibited. For eight years, Deborah produced an Artist *Beit Midrash*, a workshop where artists generate new work in dialogue with Jewish texts and scholarship. Deborah was also a mentor in the art of Jewish papercutting through a grant from the New Jersey State Council for the Arts.  
  
In papercutting, Deborah found a way to merge her work as an artist and her Jewish heritage. “I began to search through texts, through the Bible and prayer for visual imagery,” she said. “Through that search, I began to discover how rich and full these writings were.  I wanted to communicate that wealth by releasing the words, through my art, into pictorial space". Her interest in Jewish marriage contracts (*ketubot*) led her to study Hebrew and English calligraphy and the art of illuminated manuscripts.  
  
Ugoretz creates work in cut paper for organizations and book covers, Jewish marriage contracts. She also paints with acrylics and builds mobiles, small scale boxes and screens in her studio in Red Hook, Brooklyn.

title: John Lennon: Life, Legend, and Legacy
description:
A presentation by John Paul Groom

About the program 

The beginning of The Beatles took place at a summer garden fete at St. Peter's Church in Woolton, Liverpool, on July 6, 1957, marking a watershed point in music history. When John Lennon was 16 years old and performing with his skiffle band The Quarrymen, a common acquaintance called Ivan Vaughan, introduced him to Paul McCartney, who was 15 years old at the time. This one-of-a-kind partnership altered the course of music irrevocably, and our presenter will trace its history.

About the presenter

John Paul Groom gives historical presentations about the 1960s, with a particular focus on The Beatles. Originally from Liverpool, Groom resided in the same city as John Lennon and George Harrison, participated in the same Sunday school as John Lennon, and went to the same high school as Paul McCartney and George Harrison.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - November meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
**NJ Code and Coffee: Saturday, November 14th, 2-5pm at EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation Campus**

Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly NJ Code and Coffee meetup!
Coffee, good conversation, zero pressure.

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking session for people in tech and the tech-curious. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, solution architects, founders, operators, and investors are all welcome, at every skill and experience level, even first-timers and career-changers.

Most people come to chat, and some bring a laptop to work on a project. Either is welcome. It’s entirely up to you!

Come grab a coffee, meet new people, find collaborators, talk tech (or anything but tech), and take a break from the screen or the job hunt.

**Agenda**
**2:00pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3:00pm:** Networking continues
**3:00-4:00pm:** Optional career workshop in a separate space (details/RSVP here: [https://www.meetup.com/nj-code-coffee/events/317224995/](https://www.meetup.com/nj-code-coffee/events/317224995/))
**5:00pm:** Event ends
**After 5pm:** Hang out at a local brewery/restaurant (location TBD, we’ll announce it at the event)

The workshop is totally optional. Skip it and keep chatting if you’d prefer. If you do join, please plan to arrive on time and stay for the full hour.

**The Intro Circle**
Around 2:30pm, we’ll stand in a circle for a few organizer announcements, then go around the room. Keep it to 10 seconds or less, and share whichever of these apply to you:

* Your name and your role, job title, or tech stack
* What you can help others with
* What you’d like help with
* Whether you’re hiring, or looking for work.

Nervous about speaking up? A name and one sentence is plenty. After the circle, everything is self-organized.

**Details**

* Cost: Free!
* Coffee and light refreshments provided

**Community Discord: come hang out before and after!**
[https://www.codeandcoffee.chat](https://www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
EqualSpace is a shared workspace in downtown Newark, built with multicultural business owners in mind. It offers startups resources, programming, and a strong network of founders and collaborators. Learn more: [https://equalspace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: Newburgh Beacon Hudson Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point hike, the next in our Hudson River Series from one of the spots where we previously left off!
There is a whole lot to see when walking though along trails, back streets, and towns on the Hudson River.
This time, much of the route will be the sort of proposed extension of the Highlands Trail from where it currently terminates at Cornwall on Hudson to Beacon.
We'll meet at the Memorial Park parking lot at Fishkill Ave and Robert Cahill intersection. From there, we'll shuttle with as few cars as possible to our beginning point in Cornwall on Hudson.
We'll pass through a little town park at the beginning, and then follow back streets to Dock Hill and the Highlands Trail route.
We will reach Donahue Memorial Park, and then hike along the waterfront a bit.
Next, we have to follow the Shore road for a bit, which is pleasant, and then side trip over to Plum Point Park and Sloop Hill Unique Area. There are two loops there, and excellent views on the Hudson River featuring the Twin Sentinels of Storm King Mountain and Breakneck Ridge in prominent view.
We'll make our way back to the west, and pass though cemeteries including Woodland and Calvary.
We then head back down to the waterfront and possibly stop at Newburgh Brewing Company. We'll visit a famous headquarters of George Washington, and then make our way along the waterfront north toward the Newburgh-Beacon Bridge.
This is one of the bridges we have never done the walkway on, so we'll cross the Hudson here.
Once on the other side, we'll follow side streets down to and through Beacon Memorial Park where we finish.
This promises to be another interesting and diverse hike.
Distance will be about 15 miles.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Side By Side: Delving into Israeli and Palestinian Narratives, Part II
location: Congregation Shomrei Emunah, 67 Park St, Montclair, NJ 07042, USA, Social Hall
description:
**Side By Side: Delving into Israeli and Palestinian Narratives, Part II**  
A Learning Series led by Rabbi Justus Baird    
  
A three-part series exploring dual narratives of events in Israel/Palestine, specifically from Israeli Jewish and Palestinian points of view. The goal of the series is not to debate those narratives nor change our own, but simply to hear and engage with them.  
  
In this session, we will focus on narratives of the early Zionist movement and Jewish immigration, up to and including the Balfour Declaration and its impact (1880s - 1920).   
  
Advance reading, approximately two book chapters, is required. Please register so that Rabbi Justus can share pre-reading materials with you before the class.     
  
**Registration**: https://shomrei.easyshul.com/events/6ac90befe0b01c00261147e5  
  
Participants should expect the learning to be challenging and difficult, emotionally and psychologically.  
  
This session is open to all, whether you attended Part I of the series or not.   
  
The first session, on May 17, covered the establishment of the State of Israel, what Palestinians call the Naqba. The third and final session, scheduled for January 10, will explore the First Intifada.  
  
Please remember to bring your fob to access the building.  
  
**Questions?**  
Contact the Shomrei Office  
office@shomrei.org  
(973) 746-5031

title: The Fall St. James Chamber Music Concert
location: St. James Episcopal Church, 581 Valley Rd., Montclair, NJ, 07043, United States
description:
St James Episcopal Church is excited to announce that this coming Sunday November 15th at 4PM it will host a chamber music concert featuring the renowned violinist Naoko Tanaka, along with 10 other esteemed musicians. Ms Tanaka will be performing “The Lark Ascending” by Ralph Vaughan Williams. 
Also on the program are works by Bach, Poulenc, Persichetti, Beethoven and Dvorak. 
Naoko Tanaka has given concert tours as a soloist and chamber musician in the U.S., South America, Europe, Asia and Canada. A former member of The Theater Chamber Players of The Kennedy Center and The Orpheus Chamber Orchestra, she is a current member of the New York Philomusica and serves as concert master of St Luke’s Chamber Ensemble. She is on the faculty at the Juilliard School, Brooklyn College Conservatory of Music, and The Aspen Music School during the summer. She has recorded for Deutsche Gramophone, Columbia Records, and Music Masters.
St James Episcopal Church is at 581 Valley Road in Upper Montclair.

title: Gettysburg: From the Aftermath to the Address
location: Montclair Women’s Club, 82 Union Street, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Victorian Society in America 
Northern New Jersey Chapter 
VSA-NNJ meets monthly from September to June for lectures and events 
related to 19th Century history, usually on the third Monday of the month. 
Gettysburg: From the Aftermath to the Address 
presented by Greg Caggiano 
Monday, November 16, 2026 at 7:00 PM
Montclair Women’s Club
82 Union Street, Montclair NJ 
This venue is handicap accessible. Parking is available behind the building 
and on the street. Light refreshments, coffee and tea will be served. 
The program is free for members, and $10 for guests. 
In July 1863, Gettysburg had a population of 2,000 and was inundated with over 160,000 Union and Confederate soldiers. The largest battle of the war ravaged the town, leaving behind thousands of dead, farmlands turned red, and homes destroyed. This presentation focuses on aspects of the battle not normally discussed, which is the civilian experience and the aftermath of battle. Learn about the burying of bodies, establishment of the National Cemetery, and the events leading to Lincoln’s famous address. Due to graphic images and descriptions of the deceased, viewer discretion is advised. 
Greg Caggiano is an author and historian who lives in Monmouth County and has been interested in the American Civil War since childhood. He served on the Board of Directors for the Atlantic Highlands Historical Society from 2014-2023, which is housed at the 1893 Strauss Mansion Museum. Greg frequently lectures on Victorian Era subjects at Brookdale Community College and to organizations around New Jersey. 
For more information, please contact 
christinapmayer@gmail.com 
973-886-9956 
Visit us online at www.vsa-nnj.com

title: Tech Talks: Fact-Checking & Misinformation
description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.

All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.

This week's topic is: Fact-Checking & Misinformation

title: Open Book, Open Mind; Patrick Radden Keefe, "London Falling: A Mysterious Death in a Gilded City and a Family's Search for Truth"
location: Montclair - Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
NEW VENUE! Two New Yorker staff writers in conversation! The bestselling, prize-winning author of "Say Nothing" and "Empire of Pain," Patrick Radden Keefe will talk about his new true crime account, "London Falling," with D.T. Max ("Finale"). When a 19-year-old boy fell to his death in the Thames early one morning, his grieving family discovered the secret life which had drawn him into the criminal underworld that lies beneath London’s surface. 

This is a ticketed event at the Unitarian Universalist Congregation at Montclair. Tickets cost $40 and include a pre-signed copy of the book. Register at tinyurl.com/OBOMKeefe26  Books will be available for pickup at Watchung Booksellers from or you can pick up your copy of the book on November 17.  Doors open at 6:30 p.m.

“A 19-year-old man posing as the son of a Russian oligarch leaps to his death from a luxury apartment on the River Thames. That's the heart-stopping opening of Patrick Radden Keefe's 'London Falling.' Keefe investigates the death of the young imposter, as well as the role modern London played in his demise...Keefe is an exhaustive investigative reporter who spins seamless tales. He also uses the man's mysterious death to explore the criminal culture that lies just beneath the glittering surface of Britain's capital...London Falling rings true.--NPR

Open Book / Open Mind is sponsored by Montclair Public Library Foundation, Watchung Booksellers, Anonymous, David and Mary Lee Jones, and our individual Underwriters. We are also grateful for the generous support of our in-kind sponsors, First Congregational Church of Montclair, The George, and Amanti Vino. To support Open Book / Open Mind and other library programs, click here to donate.

title: Tuesday Night Open Studio Figure Drawing
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
There will be 2 more figure drawing sessions at 356 Bloomfield Ave location on November 17 and 24.  There will be no sessions in December. 
Regular Tuesday night sessions will resume in January at the new location in Wellmont Plaza. 
Tuesdays, 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space | All skill levels welcome 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in person. 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different model – usually nude, and sometimes clothed – serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say, observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a supportive community of seekers, artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies – charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. 
Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Please note: the timing of Timing Option A will go back one hour from Sat Nov 7th onwards to 6AM PDT / 9AM EDT**

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: The Avoidant Writer: Discussion and Workshop
description:
Hosted by Kim Marsh, The Open Book Company
What are you avoiding when it comes to your writing? 
Writers of all genres, interests, and experience levels are welcome to join this two-part reflective workshop.

We’ve all experienced shame, self-doubt, and fear when it comes to sharing our words with others. 

What does it feel like to name those emotions and our own inner critics? What does it look like to examine what we may be avoiding because of it? 

Are you ready to explore the stories you’ve been putting off or keeping tucked away? 

The session will be conducted in two parts. 

Part 1: A Brief Discussion and Q&A. Join book coach and editor Kim Marsh as she facilitates a discussion about the vulnerability of sharing your stories (and what goes on behind-the-scenes) with the world. 

Part 2: A Journaling Workshop. Following the discussion and Q&A, the time will become yours for independent writing. You will be provided with a few “avoidant writer” prompts and have an opportunity to reflect on something (writing-related or otherwise) you have been avoiding. While an outcome might be more clarity on how to move forward, the goal is simply to reflect and explore. 

No preparation required. Please bring your preferred writing tools: notebook, pen, and/or laptop etc. 

This workshop is here as a reminder that none of us are truly alone on this (writing) journey. 

Kim Marsh is a writing & book coach and editor. She founded The Open Book Company to help individuals find, hone and use their voice. She does this through a coaching practice rooted in empathy, authenticity, and self-compassion. The authors she works with go on to publish books with impact, meaning, and purpose.

In addition to providing one-on-one coaching, editing services and publishing support, Kim runs a global writing community, creating a space for grounding and accountability to anyone experiencing self-doubt or a desire for more support when it comes to their writing process. Kim firmly believes you don’t need a major book deal, a spot on a global stage or a PhD in English Lit to have a story worth telling. She is the editor (and a contributing author) of the anthology Avoided No More: On Writing Through Struggle, Shame, and Self-Doubt and launched her indie publishing imprint, Plymouth James Press, in 2025. She lives in Montclair, NJ.

title: Zoom: Successfully Navigating College Admissions
description:
Register HERE





We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores, and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and how to successfully navigate today’s changing landscape.

 

The session will cover current college admissions trends and strategies, the evolving test optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find the right fit, and key timelines and action steps that can make this fall productive while easing stress around the college admissions process.

 

We will also take a close look at the holistic admissions review process, including what admissions officers value when evaluating applicants and how students can develop a strong personal narrative that reflects their strengths, interests, character, and experiences.

 

Another focus will be on the role of community service and the growing importance of meaningful “passion projects.” We will discuss how students can turn their interests, values, and experiences into authentic activities that foster personal growth, demonstrate character, and show positive impact. Admissions officers place great emphasis on character, and thoughtful service can help students show initiative, empathy, and a genuine commitment to helping their communities.

 

This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens. It provides a clear and strategic overview of what students should prioritize this fall for a successful college admissions journey and how to approach the process with confidence and less stress.

 

The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www.standoutforcollege.com).

title: The Corner Book Club Meeting
description: Join us for a lively, librarian-led discussion of award-winning author Claire Keegan's novel, Small Things like These.  It is 1985 in a small Irish town. title: Youth Mental Health First Aid Training for ADULTS - November 2026
description:
Youth Mental Health First Aid is designed for adults who regularly interact with young people ages 12–18. It teaches parents, caregivers, family members, teachers, school staff, and other caring adults how to recognize and respond to mental health or substance use challenges and support a young person who may be experiencing a crisis. 
The Course will: 

Introduce common mental health challenges for youth
Review typical adolescent development
Teach a 5-step action plan for how to help young people in both crisis and non-crisis situations


Participants will receive certification after completion of all pre and post work, as well as 4 live virtual training sessions.
Registration closes 11/10.

title: International Movie Day
description:

title: Tech Talks: Fact-Checking & Misinformation
description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.

All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.

description:
Never swam before? No problem! These lessons will give you the important foundational skills in swimming and help you be more comfortable in the pool. Learn how to use proper breath control, float, and swim with a kickboard. 
 
Skills Focus:

Being comfortable in the water
Learning how to float on your back and front
Learning how to kick off the wall with a kickboard
Introducing proper breath control in the water

title: Book Talk: Power Lines: Maps That Shaped the Way We See the World by Peter Keating
description:
All maps show us where we are. Some maps also try to tell us what to think—and that’s where things get really interesting. In Power Lines: Maps That Shaped the Way We See the World (Black Dog & Leventhal, 2026), award-winning journalist Peter Keating presents a collection of maps that have defined borders, influenced social policy, and enacted political
change. In Power Lines, Keating argues that the most dramatic and influential of all maps are political maps. Rather than reflecting geographical reality, political maps express man-made boundaries, territorial claims, and national identity. All the maps in Power Lines share two qualities: historical significance and persuasive power. Travel to ancient Greece to define existence; to the age of Exploration to express borders, identities, and ambitions; to antebellum America to track the ideas that paved the path to the Civil War; to the 1884 Berlin Conference to see Western leaders carve up Africa. See the map of Adolf Hitler’s speaking engagements in 1933 that looks like a rock concert tour poster. Maps of gerrymandering. Of redlining. Of military targets and of peace treaties. The map of the world—distortions and all—that hangs on thousands of classroom walls. And the polarizing red-and-blue election
results maps that Americans are confronted with every two years. From dominion to exploration and national definition to partitions to social and ideological movements to persuasion and war, in striking images and riveting stories that span continents and centuries, Keating makes a compelling case for why, in the age of the internet, the power of political maps is unmatched, and is as potent as ever.

About the Author
Peter Keating is the author of Power Lines: Maps That Shaped the Way We See the World (Black Dog & Leventhal, 2026), which received a starred review from Publishers Weekly. He is a narrative journalist whose wide- ranging coverage of sports, finance, politics, and history has been featured in publications such as GQ, Mother Jones, National Geographic, and
Politico. He has written four national columns, including “The Biz” and “Numbers” for ESPN, where he was part of teams that won three National Magazine Awards. A 10-time winner of New York Press Club awards, Keating was a founding member of ESPN’s Investigative Unit, where his longform projects included pieces that exposed for the first time how the NFL dealt with brain injuries. From 2022 to 2025, he co-hosted the Underdogs podcast. He has also written Dingers! A Short History of the Long Ball (ESPN Books, 2006). He lives in Montclair, N.J., with his wife Karen, their daughters Ellie and Samantha, and their dog, Otis. Follow him on X at @PeterKeatingNJ.

title: Epic Worlds and Celestial Prophecies: Exploring the Between Earth and Sky Trilogy with Rebecca Roanhorse
description:
Step into a sprawling world of celestial magic, political intrigue, and ancient prophecies with New York Times bestselling author Rebecca Roanhorse as we dive deep into her acclaimed Between Earth and Sky trilogy. Black Sun, Fevered Star, and Mirrored Heavens are inspired by the rich and diverse cultures of the pre-Columbian Americas, reshaping modern speculative fiction with unmissable worldbuilding.

Black Sun, the first book in the trilogy, introduces us to the holy city of Tova. The winter solstice is usually a time for celebration and renewal, but this year it coincides with a solar eclipse, a rare celestial event proscribed by the Sun Priest as an unbalancing of the world.

Meanwhile, a ship launches from a distant city bound for Tova and set to arrive on the solstice. The captain of the ship, Xiala, is a disgraced Teek whose song can calm the waters around her as easily as it can warp a man’s mind. Her ship carries one passenger. Described as harmless, the passenger, Serapio, is a young man, blind, scarred, and cloaked in destiny. As Xiala well knows, when a man is described as harmless, he usually ends up being a villain.

Whether you are a longtime fan of the trilogy or searching for your next immersive fantasy read, this is an event you won’t want to miss out on.

Register today to go behind the scenes with one of speculative fiction's most exciting voices!

 

About the Author: 

Rebecca Roanhorse is a New York Times bestselling and Nebula, Hugo, and Locus Award-winning speculative fiction writer. She has published multiple award-winning short stories and novels, including two novels in The Sixth World series, Star Wars: Resistance Reborn, Race to the Sun for the Rick Riordan imprint, and the Hugo Award-winning epic fantasy trilogy Between Earth and Sky. She was the guest editor of America’s Best Science Fiction and Fantasy (2023) and a contributor to the New York Times “100 Best Books of the 21st Century.” She has also written for Marvel comics and games, and her TV writing includes FX’s A Murder at the End of the World, and the Marvel series Echo for Disney . She has had her own work optioned by Paramount, Amazon Studios, Netflix, and AMC Studios.

description:

Julie is haunted by her grief after living through a tragic auto wreck that claimed the life of her composer husband and young daughter. Her initial reaction is to withdraw from her relationships, lock herself in her apartment and suppress her pain. But avoiding human interactions on the bustling streets of Paris proves impossible, and she eventually meets up with Olivier, an old friend who harbors a secret love for her, and who could draw her back to reality.

ABOUT THE INSTRUCTOR
MARK PHELAN - I am a lifelong film fanatic who eats, breathes, sleeps and drinks movies. I have studied with Donald Spoto at the New School in NYC and have a BA and MA in Speech and Theatre from MSU. I am currently working as an adjunct professor teaching, among other courses, Introduction to Cinema.

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: Parish Hike and Potluck
description: Join us for abeautiful hike to Tripod Rock, located at the Pyramid Mountain Natural HistoricArea in Montville. We will meet at the church parking lot at 8:45am tocaravan or carpool to the trailhead. The hike should take about 2 1/2 hours.Wear sturdyshoes and bring water,snacks, and hiking poles (if you have them). Dogs are welcome on the trails butmust be kept on leash at all times. Potluck at Church after hike!MOREINFORMATION ABOUT THE PARISH HIKE:The 3-mile loophike begins with a 300 foot climb along the Blue Trail, where we will berewarded with an unobstructed view of the New York City skyline. (It's a prettysteep climb, but once we get to the top it's mostly flat.) We will continue onthe Blue trail to the Blue Dot trail which leads to a unique glacial erraticknown as Tripod Rock. This renowned, multi-ton boulder is balanced on threesmall boulders, and was deposited by the Wisconsin Glacier over 18,000 years ago.We will then backtrack to the Blue Trail, descend another steep climb and walkalongside the Taylortown Reservoir.  For over 10,000 years, this wildernessland provided shelter and served as a hunting, fishing, and gathering site forthe Lenape Indians, who may have used Tripod Rock as a celestialcalendar. Later, notorious outlaws used the region as a hide-out, while 19thcentury explorers and traders came and went.  At theconclusion of the hike (which is rated "Moderate") we can check outthe visitor’s center which features Indian artifacts and other exhibits. Joinfor potluck at the Church after that!Sign-up in theFellowship Hall or email Father Jerry at rector@holyspiritverona. Questions?See parishioner Ruth Portela.
source: Church of the Holy Spirit Verona

title: [Outside Org]  Aging in Montclair Saturday Social
description:
Program Title

Yankee Stadium: From the (Organ) Bench with Ed Alstrom

Program Description

Join Aging in Montclair (AIM) for a special behind-the-scenes look at Yankee Stadium with Ed Alstrom, the New York Yankees' longtime weekend organist.

Now in his 23rd season at Yankee Stadium, Ed will share fascinating stories from the organ bench, demonstrate how he brings music to life during games, and reveal how his performances enhance the excitement and atmosphere of America's favorite pastime.

A graduate of Westminster Choir College, Ed has enjoyed an extraordinary musical career. He has performed with legendary artists including Bette Midler, Chuck Berry, Leonard Bernstein, Odetta, and Dion. He also served as associate conductor for Broadway's Hairspray, directed music Off-Broadway, and released two acclaimed blues albums.

Whether you're a lifelong Yankees fan, a baseball enthusiast, or simply curious about the music behind the game, this engaging presentation offers a unique perspective on one of baseball's most beloved traditions.

 

Presented by Aging in Montclair (AIM).

title: Winter Seed Sowing Workshop
location: Glen Ridge - Meeting Room, Glen Ridge Free Public Library
description:
You don't have to wait until Spring to plan your garden -- in fact, Winter is the best time to start native seeds.

Native plants are a beautiful, beneficial addition to any garden. And growing plants from seed is an easy, low cost way to add native plants to your landscaping. In this free workshop, using seeds from the Glen Ridge Native Seed Library, learn how to prepare your native seeds so they are ready to grow next Spring. This process is called cold stratification, which will be explained with a how-to demonstration of the various methods you can use. Choose from 90 New Jersey native species and get recommendations for your yard based on growing conditions, color, and height. Learn how to grow native plants with confidence and best practices for supporting wildlife in your yard.

Sponsored by the Glen Ridge Environmental Advisory Committee.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Cali Immersive Residency: The Hands Free & Dance Heginbotham —The Party Scene
description:
Exquisitely eclectic quartet The Hands Free and members of the fabulously whimsical Dance Heginbotham join forces in The Party Scene. Inspired by The Nutcracker and your holiday office party, this music and dance extravaganza is part Drosselmeyer and part Turkey Lurkey Time. Lightly immersive and family-friendly, The Party Scene features student party guests from Montclair State University. All guests are encouraged to don impressively festive seasonal sweaters.
About The Hands Free: The Hands Free is an acoustic quartet, bringing together the creative voices of composer/performers James Moore (guitar & banjo), Caroline Shaw (violin), Nathan Koci (accordion), and Eleonore Oppenheim (bass). Drawing from an eclectic array of influences in classical, jazz, and folk traditions, the group produces a unique and evocative blend of joyful melodies, lush sonic textures, and explosive improvisations.
About Dance Heginbotham: Dance Heginbotham (DH) is a New York-based contemporary dance company committed to supporting, producing, and performing the work of choreographer John Heginbotham. With an emphasis on collaboration, DH enriches national and international communities through its unique blend of inventive, thoughtful, and rigorous dance-theater works. Founded in 2011, DH had its world premiere in January 2012 at The Kennedy Center and has been presented by major venues throughout the US, including Bard SummerScape, Brooklyn Academy of Music, Hopkins Center for the Arts, Jacob’s Pillow Dance Festival, The Joyce Theater, Lincoln Center, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, and Works Process at The Guggenheim, among many others. DH has shared the stage with luminaries of the music world, including Alarm Will Sound, Brooklyn Rider, The Knights, National Symphony Orchestra, Joshua Bell, André de Ridder, and Eric Jacobsen, and has commissioned new scores from composers Tyondai Braxton, Ethan Iverson, and Colin Jacobsen. DH has collaborated with designers and artists Maira Kalman, Isaac Mizrahi, Amy Trompetter, Maile Okamura, and Nicole Pearce in the creation of new works.
www.danceheginbotham.org 
Learn more about the Cali Immersive Residency Program at Montclair's Cali School of Music

title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series
description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series, beginning Monday, September 14.
This 10-week workshop series offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala and are open to students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University. No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required.
Mondays, beginning September 145:30–7:30 p.m.Cole Hall, Room 14110-week series
We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us. Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at  calarotaa@montclair.edu

title: Native American Sovereignty, Tribal Recognition and Environmental Justice in NJ NEW
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. You can register here.

This class will introduce the work of the New Jersey Center for Indigenous Justice (NJCIJ) at Montclair State University. The NJCIJ walks in partnership with Tribal communities to re-Indigenize New Jersey by immersing students in holistic educational experiences and transforming how Montclair State University lives up to its responsibility to society. We will explore the meanings of tribal sovereignty and give examples of how our work on environmental justice exemplifies attention to tribal priorities and future-oriented work defined by a need for broader healing and understanding in our state.

title: Spiritual Enrichment Group: Advent Program
description: Our Spiritual Enrichment Group is now meeting on the third Monday of the month at 7pm via Zoom. For many years we met at 11:45am (originally in-person and since the pandemic) via Zoom. In Spring 2026, Reverend Katherine sent the following message to our Church lay leaders: "Coffee hour is growing and newcomers are still walking through our doors. It is the only time that clergy has an opportunity to interact and be available to the congregation. Hanging around during clean up is a further opportunity as well. Exiting into an office with a closed door does not seem appropriate anymore."And so, members of the Spiritual Enrichment Group agreed to try meeting on Monday evenings; we use the Sunday Morning Worship Zoom Link. In certain seasons, we'll host a more regular (weekly) gathering using an agreed upon program. If you have any questions, speak with Reverend Katherine.
source: Church of the Holy Spirit Verona

title: Mental Health Support Group (NAMI's Connection Recovery Peer Support Group)
description:
The Essex-Passaic Chapter of NAMI (The National Alliance on Mental Illness) Connection Recovery Peer Support Group Program meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month at the West Caldwell Library on 30 Clinton Road. 

NAMI is the most influential organization devoted to helping people with mental illness and their relatives and loved ones recover and deal with mental health issues. These meetings will be led by people having some form of mental illness. During these meetings, we will conduct peer support though all people interested in this organization are encouraged to attend. You do not have to sign up in advance. All meetings are kept confidential and are led by people specifically trained to conduct these meetings.

 NAMI Connection is a recovery peer support group program that offers respect, understanding, encouragement and hope. NAMI Connection groups are:

·       Free and confidential

·       Held monthly for 90 minutes  

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.  

 

https://nami.org/Home

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Please note: the timing of Timing Option A will go back one hour from Sat Nov 7th onwards to 6AM PDT / 9AM EDT**

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

As always, we will go at a moderate pace and won’t leave anyone behind. But please be considerate of others if you don't think you will be able to hike/walk at a moderate pace for the duration.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Ping Pong Party - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
We're a group of people who will casually hit the ball around and rotate playing to 10 or 15 points for two to three hours. We may do king of the hill, round robin, a small tournament or some other organized games. Comment below with your interests and ideas!

All are welcome!! It's just casual fun! Come anytime! We're not in a league and are not here to analyze your form.

We'll be heading indoors to the table tennis tables at Ready to Golf, 3 New Bridge Road in River Edge. We'll likely have pizza delivered or hang out some more at a nearby diner or bar.

Ready to Golf has a lot to offer, including rentable table tennis tables, and comes as a recommendation of Joe, one of our many regulars.

We'll be reserving 5-6 tables for singles and doubles play but we may get more if they're available and if more than 30 people show up. When out playing, make sure to include others if people are waiting off to the side.

The rental price covers paddles and balls. Final pricing will be somewhere in the neighborhood of $10-15 per person. Please bring cash to pay for what you owe! We'll settle the bill before play.

If you're stopping by later than 8:15 p.m., please let me know by commenting below, or calling or texting me. That would be helpful for planning purposes.

There is a snack bar on site open until 7:30 p.m. There are some bottled drinks available and a water fountain. But you're welcome to bring food and beverages from the outside. It's BYOB friendly. There's also plenty of seating and space for hanging out on the side when not playing and some televisions with sports programming.

If interested in learning more about the place, here's the website: www.readytogolf.com

Hope you'll join us for our seventh ping pong event. Questions, comments, concerns or having trouble finding us? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at 201-234-9609.

If interested, check out one of our many other events. We do bowling, volleyball, tennis, soccer, hiking, martial arts, billiards, dancing and bar crawls: [www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball](https://www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball)

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

description: Death of Caesar Fine Arts Gallery hosts J Read's "Art of the REadMIX" production. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Accounting Society - KPMG
description:
KPMG is a prominent global network of independent firms delivering professional audit, tax, and advisory services. As one of the prestigious "Big Four" accounting firms, it operates across roughly 140 countries and employs over 270,000 professionals worldwide. The organization was officially formed in 1987 through the merger of Peat Marwick International and Klynveld Main Goerdeler, with its name representing the initials of its foundational partners. Instead of functioning as a single multinational corporation, KPMG is structured as a network of distinct, locally managed member firms. Its primary client base includes major corporations, government agencies, and non-profit institutions seeking regulatory compliance and strategic business consulting. Through this decentralized model, the firm maintains a massive footprint in global financial compliance and corporate restructuring.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Sparks, Shadows, and Epic Romantasy with Helen Scheuerer
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/224402



Join us virtually for a downright intoxicating conversation with bestselling fantasy author Helen Scheuerer as we delve into her thrilling new novel, Kiss of the Black Flame.

Some bargains are sealed with blood. Others with fire. The deadliest are sealed with a kiss...

Saige Grayson has always believed stories could heal—even when her own body refuses to. As the most promising bookbinder in the capital, she’s learned to work through chronic pain and crushing debt, restoring other people’s treasures while trying not to fall apart herself. But when the man she owes decides her rare talent is worth more than her payments, Saige is traded to the Azkari—an immortal race forged by the gods for war—and imprisoned in their ancient stronghold.

Her only chance of survival lies with Archer, a fallen Azkari general imprisoned beside her—cursed, dangerous, and impossible to ignore. He offers her a way out, and in return, Saige must help him retrieve and restore an ancient book. But the book is made of living magic, powerful enough to stop a great evil—or unleash it. And as Saige works with Archer, the tome begins to awaken something dark and dangerous—both in the realm and within her.

As their enemies close in and buried memories resurface, Saige and Archer must decide what they’re willing to sacrifice: their freedom, their fragile trust…or the spark that could ignite the world.

Register now to take part in the magic–and the spice–of Helen’s newest book!

About the Author: 

Helen Scheuerer is a Sunday Times (London) bestselling author best known for her romantasy series, The Legends of Thezmarr and The Ashes of Thezmarr. Her work has been highly praised for its strong, flawed female characters and its action-packed plots. Helen’s love of writing and books led her to pursue a creative writing degree and a Master's of Publishing. She has been a full-time author since 2018 and is constantly dreaming up new stories.

title: 🥾 Let's Hike!! at Garret Mountain
description:
Let's Walk!!
Garret Mountain Yellow and White Loop Trail is a heavily trafficked loop trail located near Woodland Park, New Jersey that features a lake and is good for all skill levels. The trail offers a number of activity options and is best used from March until October.

**PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES EARLY SO WE CAN START ON TIME!**

We will hike a moderate 3 miles. This is **not** a paved trail, please do **not** wear sneakers.

We will meet in the **Auto Overlook** parking lot. It’s a one way, you will pass the equestrian, Lambert Tower before reaching the sign for AUTO OVERLOOK.

As always, we will go at a moderate pace and won’t leave anyone behind. But **please be considerate** of others if you don't think you will be able to hike at a moderate pace for the duration.

[https://www.google.com/maps/place/Parking+lot,+Paterson,+NJ+07503/@40.9057189,-74.1750062,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2fdd38a2aa1a1:0x526711cb124756e2!8m2!3d40.905813!4d-74.1750982!16s%2Fg%2F11fx7w406f?hl=en-US&entry=ttu](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Parking+lot,+Paterson,+NJ+07503/@40.9057189,-74.1750062,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2fdd38a2aa1a1:0x526711cb124756e2!8m2!3d40.905813!4d-74.1750982!16s%2Fg%2F11fx7w406f?hl=en-US&entry=ttu)

Rain or extreme weather will cancel the event.

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: The Space for Words - Literary Open mic with NJ Poetry Circle
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
The Space for Words – Literary Open mic hosted with the NJ Poetry Circle
Saturday December 5  |  Doors open at 7:30, start time 8 pm  |  $10 for everyone 
This event is usually held on the last Friday of every month.  The Space is transitioning to a new location, so this schedule is different through the end of the year.  We will resume the last Friday schedule at the new location in Wellmont Plaza in January. 
Hey writers, poets, and storytellers!  Come share your art with us at The Space for Words Open Mic Night. Whether you’re a seasoned author or just getting started, this is your chance to share your work in front of a supportive and inspiring audience. 
Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work — the stage is yours! The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Each performer gets a maximum of 5 minutes to read, and at the end we take time to socialize and vibe with one another. 
Come for the words, stay for the community. The Space for Words has grown into an amazing community of writers supporting one another. This event is open to all levels and all genres, so whether you write fiction, non-fiction, memoir, or poetry, we want to hear from you. It’s all about celebrating the power of storytelling in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. All of our open mic nights are always inclusive. 
Anyone who puts their name in the bucket upon entry gets a shot at the mic, and has a maximum of 5 minutes. Depending on how many people sign up and if time allows, we can have people come up a second time. 
Audience members are, as always, a welcome and vital part of these performances. 
If you have published books that you would like to sell, bring some copies and be prepared to accept payment. 
General guidelines: 

Hate speech of any kind is never allowed and will be shut down.
Violence or references to physical harm to others will be shut down.

BYOB is welcome, and some light snacks and drinks are served. 
Accessibility: The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building, accessible via a flight of stairs. Unfortunately, there is no elevator access at this time. This means we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs or guests with significant mobility challenges. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are almost finished!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site.

Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). title: Folk & Blues with Tal Naccarato
description:
About the program

A singer-songwriter and guitarist in the Americana, folk, and blues styles, Tal Naccarato plays solo acoustic music from his original and traditional repertoire. Mixed into the performance are discussions of the various music styles and demonstrations of rare vintage instruments. 

 

About the artist

Tal Naccarato is a vibrant composer, songwriter, and teaching artist whose roots stretch from the medieval mountain village of Fiumefreddo, Bruzio, Italy, to the vibrant community of East Flatbush, Brooklyn. His original music is a mix of folk, Americana, rock, and blues, mixed with classical guitar elements and a distinct bluesy swing. Tal was the first-place winner in the Long Island Blues Society Solo/Duo Competition in 2023. He performs solo acoustic shows, both with original music and traditional songs.

title: Chamber Opera Performance: "L'enfant et les Sortilèges"
description:
Maurice Ravel’s L’enfant et les sortilèges is a wildly imaginative fantasy opera where a single child’s tantrum sets an entire enchanted world into motion. In a flash of frustration, the ordinary becomes extraordinary—walls start to whisper, teacups burst into song, animals argue back, and the child’s room transforms into a living, breathing world of magic and mischief.
As this fantastical realm awakens, the child is swept into a dazzling swirl of musical surprises and unexpected voices, where every object has something to say and nothing is quite as it seems. With Ravel’s shimmering, kaleidoscopic score at its heart, this enchanting opera is a playful journey through wonder, chaos, and the power of imagination to transform everything it touches.
(Sung in French with English Surtitles~ runtime: approx 1 hour)

title: Civic Leadership and SEL: Lessons from NJ Changemakers with New Jersey Hall of Fame
description:
Civic Leadership and SEL: Lessons from NJ Changemakers invites educators to explore how the powerful, personal stories of New Jersey Hall of Fame inductees can serve as catalysts for meaningful social-emotional learning and authentic civic engagement in today’s classrooms. By examining moments of courage, empathy, advocacy, and ethical decision-making in the lives of New Jersey leaders, educators will uncover practical ways to help students build self-awareness, social awareness, and a sense of agency.
Drawing from the lives and legacies of Peter J. McGuire (Father of Labor Day), Dorothea Dix (mental health reformer), David Mixner (political activist, author, and playwright), and Clara Maass (public health pioneer), participants will analyze how these changemakers confronted injustice, advocated for vulnerable communities, and took action in times of social and public health crises—making abstract concepts such as fairness, wellness, and justice tangible and relevant for students. 
Educators will compare and contrast AI-powered lesson generators, including MagicSchool and Curipod, and create SEL or civic action lessons and student activities using inductee stories, leveraging AI scaffolding to differentiate instruction for diverse learners. This workshop empowers educators to transform local legends into catalysts for empathy, critical thinking, and civic participation—helping all students see themselves as the next generation of changemakers.

Hosted by: The ADP Center

description:
Each year, our graduating class participates in a proud Class Gift tradition where members of the class invest in the University by supporting areas of Montclair State University that are most important to them. We invite the Class of 2026 to come together to show your support!
All gifts to Montclair count! Make your gift to any area of campus you feel most passionate about – such as the Emergency Book Fund, The Red Hawk Pantry, your school or college, The Fund for Montclair State or athletic program.
Your gift will pay it forward for future Red Hawks and kick-start your philanthropic connection to Montclair.

For a gift of $40, celebrate this milestone with your family, friends and colleagues by having your message displayed on the screen at the Commencement you will be participating in, and receive a customized philanthropy cord.

Customized philanthropy cords will be available for pick-up:

Monday, October 26 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Thursday, November 2nd  from 2:00 – 4:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Tuesday, December 8 in the Student Center Lobby

Graduates can also arrange to pick up their philanthropy cords in the Overlook Corporate Center, 150 Clove Road, Little Falls, NJ during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Philanthropy cords can also be mailed to those who cannot pick it up. Please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving at stewartj@montclair.edu or 973-655-5328 to finalize options to get your cords for the Winter Commencement.
Every student has benefitted from donor generosity to areas of academic support, emergency funding for students and overall priorities to boost students’ success every day. Thank you for paying it forward!For more information, please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving, at 973-655-5328 or stewartj@montclair.edu.
